set.prevailing_wage_basis: DIR Public Works Case No. 2010-008 (April 8, 2010, CMFA conduit revenue bonds), applying PW 2004-016 Rancho Santa Fe Village Senior Affordable Housing (CSCDA conduit bonds for affordable housing): conduit bond proceeds and loan repayments never enter public coffers, so conduit bond financing is not payment out of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b). CDLAC QRRP evaluation criteria (4 CCR 5230) contain no prevailing wage condition. This covers the CMFA bonds and County TEFRA approval only; other public sources in the same deal (HOME 24 CFR 92.354 at 12+ HOME units, PBV 24 CFR 983.153(c) at 9+ units, state loans or a County fee offset) can trigger prevailing wage independently. https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2010/2010-008.pdf
set.audit_note: Tier 3: prevailing wage set false for the conduit bond itself based on DIR coverage determinations PW 2010-008 and PW 2004-016; check every other funding source in the stack separately.

reason: DIR coverage determinations hold conduit tax-exempt bond financing is not public funds under Labor Code 1720(b), so the bond alone does not trigger prevailing wage.

set.prevailing_wage_basis: No program-specific rule found. Labor Code 1720(b)(4) treats fees that are paid, reduced, waived or forgiven by a public agency as public funds, but SB 937 deferral only changes timing and is not listed; ADU fee reductions and any Program C-5 reduction could count under 1720(b)(4) subject to the 1720(c)(3) de minimis test (under $600,000 and under 2% of project cost) and the 1720(c)(1) and (c)(5) private residential exemptions. No DIR determination on fee deferral or SCIP assessment financing was located. Outcome depends on project facts. https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720
set.audit_note: Tier 3: left unclear; only the general Labor Code 1720(b)(4) definition applies and the result turns on 1720(c) exemptions and project facts.

reason: Searched Labor Code 1720, DIR coverage determinations and the City staff report and found no stated rule on whether fee deferral or SCIP financing triggers prevailing wage.
